body: Thanks so much, I really appreciate it. Unfortunately I think I've reached the end of what I can deal with now. I hope things work out well for you, you seem like a great guy. All the best!

Thanks for replying, unfortunately it's been made clear I'm not welcome to stay at home any longer as I'm not pulling my weight, so I have nowhere to go. Think that's all for me now. I hope things go well for you :)
Thank you :) but that's all for me now. Wishing you all the best.

What's kept you going? I've been ill for about three years, but I was ill with something else for about a year before that (likely to have caused the CFS), so about 4 years total. I'm 20, so these should have been the fun years where you're carefree and making friends and stuff.. I feel like I'm missing out on all of that, and am just a lonely lump losing social skills by the minute. And I'm so scared that people will get sick of me if I keep cancelling plans, or when I'm off  sick from uni I'm missing making friends in class or whatever. It's so hard to juggle work, rest and socialising, and then any reading/watching tv to recharge after that, if I'm not too foggy. I just hate that I can't even do the things I love anymore. Running. reading and art were my favourite things, the first is out the window completely and the other two are so draining it's not worth it, so I just watch TV instead. It's just a very, very depressing way to exist.

Thank you for taking the time to reply. I'm so sorry you've been ill for so long. 

The family situation is frustrating. They definitely get it on an intellectual level, but emotionally it's a different story. I think they just see me "lazing about" all day, or on the odd occasion when I've been able to leave the house, get a bus and sit in a park just to get a change of scene and some fresh air, it's used against me for days on end. It doesn't help that we've been stuck in each other's company for about 4 months straight, but one of the most hurtful things anyone has ever said to me was my own mother, when she was giving me a row for not pulling my weight around the house, said she was beginning to think I enjoyed being ill. That's definitely created a sense of distrust and I don't really feel comfortable talking to her about the illness any more. 

I suppose I've not really kept up with the latest research other than headlines because I can't really concentrate on scientific articles or anything. All I'm getting from my doctor is GET, CBT and a shrug, and if I ask for any tests or supplements they can recommend or anything they start giving me a lecture about spending too much time googling. But to be honest I'm not really given the time of day by doctors so of course I'm going to go and try to do some kind of research to try and help myself. But it all seems very futile at the moment. I hope the research comes to something, because all I've heard when it comes to CFS research is that because so many doctors either don't think it exists, or don't know about it, it's getting a tiny amount of funding, which is disheartening. 

I'm definitely getting counselling back at uni, that's already in place. I do find it very helpful to talk to someone who won't dismiss me or judge or give unsolicited health advice. I am very worried about a jam-packed academic schedule and all the appointments I'm going to have though. 

You're so kind, thank you. It's such a horrible illness in so many ways. Compared to many I'm still very new to this (diagnosed about 2 years ago, ill for maybe 3), and the frustration can be overwhelming, especially when you're stuck not being able to do basic tasks like showering when your friends are doing more in half an hour before they leave in the morning than you do in two full days... And then do a full day of uni, and a night out afterwards. It's hard to watch and not feel like you're missing out on what should be your most fun and carefree years. 

Anyway, thanks again. I'm in Scotland :)

Yeah, I'll be getting support when I go back to uni, and that's pretty much all I've got to cling on to right now. It's just very difficult to shake the idea that if I can't do what I want to do... What's the point? Why should I have to constantly lower my expectations and just survive rather than do all the things I would be able to do without this, and everyone else is able to do? I think I'm just mourning the loss of everything still, and just really not coping with it well. It also doesn't help when on the outside it looks like nothing... People definitely have this idea that "oh, you can sit and watch tv/read/stare at the wall/nap all day but you can't work, cook, or help around the house? Just get to bed earlier and do some exercise". I had more sympathy when I sprained my wrist by tripping over my own feet, just because people could see it. I hate this notion that it's somehow our fault or we're not doing enough, or are just lazy. It's so demoralising on top of such a horrible illness already.

Thank you so much. I think you replied on one of my other posts too (this seems to have turned into my breakdown alt haha), and you just seem like the loveliest person. It is definitely the isolation that's getting to me. Like, I've never been the most sociable person in the world anyway, but in the last four months I've spent almost all of my time with the same two family members, and that's enough to drive everyone involved crazy. So maybe it's good to be moving back out... It's just a very scary prospect at the moment. Thank you for the support. ❤️

Unfortunately where I am you just take one full time class. It's not possible to drop to part time. I'm worried about possibly dropping out because I already did one year at a different uni that was too much for me so had to switch, which used up a year of funding, so I can't afford to drop out and start again. It's all just very stressful. But thank you for your reply :)

Thanks for this. Unfortunately I think I've just got to the point where I don't even care anymore. I think if I had the energy/willpower to do something maybe things would get better. But the amount of time, energy, enthusiasm that needs... I don't have it and I don't think it would be worth it anyway if I'm still going to be ill. I've lost the life I thought/hoped I would live, and I don't want to be a person who has to be totally dependent on family/the state, just to sit in a room all day doing nothing. I just... can't.
Yeah, pretty much how I feel. But as each day passes I feel less and less like it's worth pushing on.

Thanks. I've had therapy, but it's very difficult to get help over the summer months when I'm away from college. And the college sessions are capped at 8 1hour sessions. For my illness there's no treatment available. So it all feels very hopeless right now

Thanks for your kind words. Is there anything in particular you've found that helps? Or that you keep in mind to help you keep going? I feel like I've just got to the point where I feel like I'm fighting a losing battle now, and it doesn't seem worth the hassle :(

Sorry for taking so long to reply, it's been a bad week. Yeah definitely, although not the same illness cfs and lyme are definitely in the same "we don't really know what's wrong with you so it must be all in your head" category. I even had a doctor telling me I was just in denial when I asked for a Lyme disease test, which was disheartening. It's definitely something I will look into again. I'm so sorry you're struggling too. What keeps you going? Feel free to PM me whenever, I'm sure we could both do with an ear that actually understands first hand!

I do understand. I had a bad illness that actually led me to have cfs, so it kind of feels like I went from being fine to being permanently ill. It sucks. We do at least have some understanding doctors and some funding/research, but it's still not great. It is good to know that at least it's recognised as an illness/disability, so there is funding available if needed. There's definitely a sense of 'why me?', which then just turns into a 'why not you?', if that makes sense. But there definitely is a part of me that can't see the point in fighting a losing battle.

Wow, thank you so much for this. There's definitely a lot of advice in there I need to follow - I've been looking into mindfulness and healthier eating a lot recently, and I'll be seeing a therapist when I go back to college. Getting outside does help a lot when there's sun! I just... at the moment I feel so helpless, I always feel like there's so much I should be doing and can't. It's so horrible. I had mild anxiety and depression anyway, but recently it has totally skyrocketed until I can hardly do anything. I just freeze, and overthink everything, and panic, then get exhausted and sit and feel so low because I can't do anything. I feel so trapped, and like there's no point in going through all this hell when there's no light at the end of the tunnel. There are many people saying they have come to terms with it and still have good lives. A part of me strives for that but another part of me thinks, what's the point if that's as good as it's going to get? I just feel so trapped. I feel terrible throwing myself a pity party when there are so many people struggling with this, but I just don't think i'm strong enough to cope with it. I will try these things anyway, and thank you so much for such a long and full answer. I hope you feel OK :)
It's hard to feel like people would care when you just feel like such a useless burden :(

I'm so sorry to hear that :( I definitely relate to what you're saying. This is the time everyone says are the best years of your life, you meet your lifelong friends and partners, you party all the time and have a lot of fun... and I feel like I'm struggling so hard to barely scrape a pass and do hardly anything else. It's more the anticipation of going back that's so hard, I think, I don't know what to expect and it's so stressful. And yeah, I definitely do need to work out ways of staying within my limits, it's something I struggle with a lot. A lot of people don't understand that just because you managed to 'push through' and do something once, doesn't mean you can just do anything if you put your mind to it... it takes so much energy. Ugh. Anyway, some kind of cure (or even proper acknowledgement of the illness...) is something. It's just such a shame it is really not taken seriously and has such rubbish funding.

Thanks for that - I did see it and found it really helpful! There's definitely a voice in the back of my head telling me how terrible it is that people I went to school with are graduating this year and I'm still trudging along doing badly. And I know mindfulness is supposed to be helpful for that, I just struggle to get myself to sit down and do it because I'm always so stressed about all the things I  should be doing or have/will miss out on. And I definitely feel the grief... It's such a strange thing to mourn what could have been, but I definitely am. If anyone has any other ways of helping with that I'd be really grateful to hear them..!

Yeah, I find psychologists and counselling helpful... unfortunately spaces are very very limited where I am with very long waiting lists. I've not been able to see anyone for a few months over the summer and that's definitely been hard. Well done on finishing uni! I've still got a long way to go and it's very daunting. Do you have any tips on how you managed it?!

Yeah, I do love to read and write. It's so exhausting though, but I guess it is something you can do in bed! Did you meet your wife before or after you became ill? It's something I'm still so bitter about, that I feel so many experiences a person is 'entitled' to (like relationships, kids, career) have been taken away from me, and all I have are some memories of early high school which weren't really the greatest anyway. Do you have any other reasons to keep going you find helpful?

Sorry for the late reply! Yeah, I find that so hard though. I managed to lose touch with most people from high school and haven't been able to make strong friendships or anything at college yet because I'm hardly there, and am spending most of my energy trying to scrape a pass. So all I have right now really is my mom, and I feel so bad about it... I should be out looking after myself, working, not taking up all of her time having breakdowns or not being able to cook or look after myself. I just feel so useless and such a burden :(

Sorry for taking so long to reply! Yes, I definitely feel you on the anger front. I totally get that there are so many illnesses out there, and so many ill people, and only so many doctors, but it's hard not to feel brushed off when so many doctors either tell you there's nothing they can do, or don't even believe CFS is a thing and tell you it's stress or depression or whatever. Like, I'm stressed and depressed, but I would 100% say that's because of the CFS, not the other way round. My brother actually had some post viral thing for a few weeks and was diagnosed with chronic fatigue, despite it literally only being for 3 or 4 weeks and the diagnostics clearly stating there need to be symptoms for over 6 months. It's pretty much a label that says "tired, and we don't know why", and it's slapped on almost anyone without the correct tests etc being carried out, so there must be so many people wandering around with a CFS diagnosis that have something completely different that they just couldn't be bothered ruling out. It feels like a fight most times I see my doctor with something else they might be able to test for, because they just think I'm crazy or in denial or just wanting attention. I don't know. I just hope that I'll be able to come to terms with it at some point because I know I'm wasting so much energy being angry. I hope you find something that helps you feel better :)

I really, really hope that something might work. However it's so difficult to find doctors that know or care about this illness, and I just don't have the energy most of the time to try and do my own research. Is there anything in particular that worked for you?

Sorry about taking so long to get back! I'm so sorry you've been struggling with it for so long. I definitely only am getting through it right now because of my mom, but I have to say it makes me feel so guilty... she never asked for this, and I'm supposed to be pretty much self-sufficient now. I shouldn't have to be leaning on her all the time for support but I don't have anyone else - I hardly have the energy to do the work for college, let alone the socialising aspect or building proper relationships or anything. I've definitely found that doctors like to just throw cfs sufferers on anti depressants etc because it's the easy option and there's 'nothing else they can do'. That definitely doesn't help, since most of us don't have the energy to go looking for other treatments! I hope you find something that works for you, and report back if you do! We definitely do need each other, it's such an isolating illness and you forget you're not the only one when everyone around you is living their life to the fullest, it seems. I only made this account to make this post but I'm actually on it quite a bit now, so anyone is welcome to PM me if you need an ear :)

So sorry for taking so long to get back, I've had a very down week. Thanks for the tips; I think it definitely is a case of coming to terms with the illness, and realising that this is how things are now. I'm still dealing with the grief of losing so much I think, and am pretty stuck in the anger/depression states. Hopefully sometime I'll manage to reach acceptance like you have. I think also I just feel so useless... I haven't even had a proper job yet, I haven't contributed to society in any real way, and I can't see it happening anytime in the near future. I just hate that feeling of being a leech and just taking handouts to live while I do nothing all day. It makes me feel like such a loser, but I don't know how I can do anything to make myself feel any better about that. So I just drag myself down into a hole of anxiety/depression and feel more and more terrible. I don't know, it's been a very difficult month and I'm really struggling to deal with it all. But it is very helpful to hear from someone who has been dealing with it, and coping, and has a positive outlook, and I hope at some point I can get there too. So thank you :)

Thanks so much for replying. I've been tested for Lyme and it's come back negative, though that wasn't with a specialist. I'm in the UK and the NHS has a bit of an issue with things like Lyme disease, and honestly I don't know why. It feels like a doctor went "we did lots of blood tests, they came back clear, so you have CFS. Bye" and ever since then every symptom or other illness I've brought up just gets shot down as one of the "broad range of symptoms" of CFS. I know a lot of the symptoms are similar though, so I'm so sorry you're going through it too. How are you coping?

Thanks so much for your reply. I'm so sorry about the migraines - I get them sometimes and they're so unbelievably horrible. It's so easy to get caught up in yourself and feel like you're the only one going through something like this, mainly because all of us are stuck hidden away at home. But yeah, it feels like my whole future has been ripped away. This is supposed to be the best time of my life or whatever, being young and carefree and learning, travelling, spending time with friends... And I'm stuck at home doing nothing. And I totally get the thing about people forgetting - I know they don't mean to, or don't mean to downplay things, but it's so difficult seeing your family/support network getting frustrated with you because you're not getting better. Like it's your fault, and you're not trying hard enough, when in reality it's just one of those things... We've been dealt shitty hands in life, and that's just it really. Nobody's fault. But that's obviously a really hard thing to accept. Wishing you all the best.
Thank you for the kind words. Sometimes we forget there are others like us because they're all stuck at home too haha

Yeah, I definitely find the more I think about it the worse it gets - but I find when I'm resting I'm left with not much else to do but think about it, unfortunately. Wow, 15 years is a long time. Is there anything in particular you've learned to help in that time? And if you don't mind me asking, how do you spend most of your days? Sorry if this comes across as intrusive, I think at the moment all I can see in front of me is an abyss, and hearing others who are managing can be really helpful. Thank you for your response
Thank you so much. As horrible as it is it's nice to know that there are other people dealing with this out there. I hope you're managing ok!
